Interface ReflectiveIntrospection<T>

Type Parameters:
T - The bean type
All Superinterfaces:
AnnotationMetadata, AnnotationMetadataDelegate, AnnotationMetadataProvider, AnnotationSource, ArgumentCoercible<T>, BeanInfo<T>, BeanIntrospection<T>, Ordered
All Known Implementing Classes:
ReflectionBeanIntrospection, SupplementedBeanIntrospection
public interface ReflectiveIntrospection<T> extends BeanIntrospection<T>
What a reflective introspection knows beyond the BeanIntrospection contract: every constructor of the type, and the members a property is made of, each with the class declaring it and its own metadata.

A specification that describes a type — the constraint metadata of Jakarta Validation, for instance — names constructors by their parameter types and distinguishes the constraints declared on a field from the ones declared on a getter, or in the type from the ones inherited from a super type. A generated introspection merges the members of a property into one metadata unless it is compiled with @Introspected(members = true); this contract always keeps them apart, and BeanIntrospection.separatesDeclarations() says so for either.

Since:
5.2.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

  • Method Details

    • getConstructors

      List<BeanConstructor<T>> getConstructors()
      Description copied from interface: BeanIntrospection
      Returns the constructors this introspection describes.

      By default an introspection only describes the constructor used to instantiate beans, in which case this method returns a singleton list containing BeanIntrospection.getConstructor(). When the introspected type opts in via Introspected.constructors(), or by annotating individual constructors with io.micronaut.context.annotation.Executable, every described constructor is returned, including its own annotation metadata and the annotation metadata of its parameters.

      A described constructor reports the parameters of its JVM signature, which for a non-static inner class means that BeanConstructor.getArguments() starts with the implicit enclosing instance, named this$0, exactly as Constructor.getParameterTypes() reports it. The enclosing instance must therefore be passed first to BeanConstructor.instantiate(Object...). BeanIntrospection.getConstructor() and BeanIntrospection.getConstructorArguments() keep the source level view and never describe it, so for a non-static inner class the first element of this list does not report the same arguments as BeanIntrospection.getConstructor().

      Specified by:
      getConstructors in interface BeanIntrospection<T>
      Returns:
      Every constructor of the type, BeanIntrospection.getConstructor() first
